paper_metadata.title: Effect of carbon on the microstructures and mechanical properties of as cast Nb-base alloy

evidence.quote: Microstructure and mechanical properties of Nb35Ti6Al5Cr8V (at.%) containing different C contents (0, 1, 11.6 at.%) were investigated.

evidence.quote: The carbide in 1% C alloy is fcc MC.

Fig. 8 shows an SEM micrograph from a compression sample of the 10C alloy, indicating that cracks initiated within the large carbides thus leading to a reduction in the ductility of the 10C alloy

In the alloys containing C, dislocations were observed, as shown in Fig. 6. Such dislocations were introduced into the Nbss during casting due to the difference in thermal expansion between the carbide and the Nbss.
Some weak streaks in the diffraction pattern suggest that the defects are planar. These defects are actually a high density of microtwins.

The alloy is only solid solution strengthened and, therefore, there is a good chance of strengthening it further by introducing precipitates or secondary particles at the expence of losing some room temperature ductility.

Such reinforcement strengthening is important for the 10C alloy because 11.6% C addition produced about 20% volume fraction of carbide, but is not important for the 1C alloy due to the small volume fraction of the carbide (~2%)
the carbides refine the grain size which will lead to an increase in yield stress via the Hall–Petch relationship, although the effect is small here
the carbides are nearly continuously precipitated at grain boundaries (Fig. 3), which could restrain boundary sliding and thus increase creep strength.

The results show that the compressive yield strength of this Nb–Ti–Al alloy was increased significantly by C addition. The addition of 1% C results in an improvement of 130 MPa in yield strength at room temperature, and 250 MPa for 11.6% C.
